source.author: verg
source.text: Ac velut ingentem formicae farris acervum cum populant, hiemis memores, tectoque reponunt; it nigrum campis agmen, praedamque per herbas convectant calle angusto; pars grandia trudunt obnixae frumenta umeris; pars agmina cogunt castigantque moras; opere omnis semita fervet.
source.text_original: Ac velut ingentem formicae farris acervum / cum populant, hiemis memores, tectoque reponunt; / it nigrum campis agmen, praedamque per herbas / convectant calle angusto; pars grandia trudunt / obnixae frumenta umeris; pars agmina cogunt / castigantque moras; opere omnis semita fervet.
source.text_english: And just as ants, when they plunder a great heap of grain, mindful of winter, and store it away beneath cover; so the black column moves across the fields, and they haul the spoil over the grass along a narrow track; some, straining, push along the large grains on their shoulders; some gather the ranks and chide the laggards; every path is alive with labor.

reuse.text: alia prouident in futurum, ut ingentem formicae farris aceruum cum populant hiemis memores tectoque reponunt, ut apes, quae patriam solae et certos nouere penates uenturaeque hiemis memores aestate laborem experiuntur et in medium quaesita reponunt .

reuse.text_english: Others make provision for the future, as when ants, mindful of winter, pillage and store up under cover a huge heap of grain; as when bees, the only creatures to know their homeland and fixed household gods, mindful of the coming winter, endure labor in summer and lay by what they have gathered in common.
